title: Pressure ulcers: site, stage and healing
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's pressure ulcer, if any.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for pressure ulcer.

HPI
Pt is an 80-year-old female presenting for evaluation of a pressure ulcer over the sacrum. Pt reports increasing discomfort and noted worsening of the area over the past week. She is currently mobile with a walker but spends significant time in a chair. Pt reports no systemic symptoms like fever or chills.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg QD
Atorvastatin 20mg QD
Aspirin 81mg QD
Multivitamin QD

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, fatigue.
Integumentary: Positive for pressure ulcer over sacrum. Denies rashes or pruritus.
MSK: Denies joint pain.
CV: Denies chest pain or palpitations.
Resp: Denies SOB or cough.
GI: Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
GU: Denies dysuria.
Neuro: Denies headache or dizziness.

Social History
Lives at home with daughter. Retired. No tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, Stroke.
Father: MI.

Vitals
BP: 132/78
HR: 74 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Ht/Wt: 54 kg

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 6.2%
eGFR: 72
WBC: 8.4
Hgb: 12.1
Plt: 210k

Exam
General: Alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Skin: Exam of sacrum reveals a stage 3 pressure ulcer. Wound measures approximately 3x4 cm. Wound bed shows some slough. Periwound skin is intact. No purulent drainage noted.
MSK: Gait steady with walker.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation.

Assessment
1. Stage 3 pressure ulcer of the sacrum.

Plan
1. Pressure ulcer management: Cleanse wound with normal saline. Apply hydrocolloid dressing to sacral site.
2. Wound care education: Instructed pt and daughter on frequent repositioning and pressure relief.
3. F/u: Return to clinic in 2 weeks for wound re-evaluation.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Pressure ulcer of the sacral region, stage 3: L89.153 (HCC 381).

distractors.why: The stage is documented: it decides the code and the HCC.
